title: Give a matching task a spare target
statement: Give a matching item more targets than prompts, without announcing which one is spare, so its last pairs can't be won by elimination.
example: A static scan of one course found 192 matching items that announced their spare target.
detail: The intake of a Grade 5 generator pilot asked for at least one unused decoy target in every matching item before scale (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0067-g5-generator-pilot-intake-and-team-async-2026-06-23.qmd`), and a test design listed its three-by-three matching item among its honest limits as a minor elimination cue (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0059-map-equivalent-test-design-v4.qmd`). A static accessibility scan of the merged Grade 5 course named 192 matching items that announce a decoy bucket (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0235-g5-course-build-pipeline-2026-06-23-to-06-30.qmd`). Let the text, rather than a common association, fix each pairing, so no pair can be won by guessing.
against: a structural grader run on one Grade 5 dataset listed an unused right bucket as a failure reason 638 times (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0068-g5-static-dataset-intake-2026-06-23.qmd`, line 116), so one local rule treated a spare target as a defect. The judge's own matching rules allowed equal counts: '- Equal or greater number of definitions/descriptions' (`icloud-work/evaluator/ap_benchmark/prompts/match.py`, line 12). The pass rates and reasons came from one model judge, with no learner data. A scan of the merged course flagged 192 match items announcing a decoy bucket (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0235-g5-course-build-pipeline-2026-06-23-to-06-30.qmd`, line 133); an announced decoy is itself a cue, so an extra target helps only when it is not announced.
